The stopping rule of the item-revision loop

Source: R/loop.R
loop_criterion.Rd

loop_criterion() makes the criterion of revision_loop(): The rule that says when items are polished. Decide it before the first run, so that the number of rounds means something. Every part gives one row in the criteria table, and the items are polished when every row passes.

Usage

loop_criterion(
  no_failing_items = TRUE,
  min = list(alpha = 0.8, own_scale = 0.9),
  max = list(careless_share = 0.05),
  min_items = 3,
  factors = FALSE,
  min_total = NULL
)

Arguments

no_failing_items

require that no item has a failing flag?

min, max

named lists of targets for stats (see above).

min_items

smallest number of items per scale.

factors

require the number of dimensions to match the number of scales?

min_total

smallest number of items in all, or NULL.

Value

A function for the criterion argument of revision_loop().

Details

  • no_failing_items: No item has a flag with severity "fail", from any step.

  • min: For each named stat, its lowest value (over scales or items) must be at least the target. The default asks for alpha of at least 0.80 in every scale and at least 90% of items closest to their own scale.

  • max: For each named stat, its highest value must be at most the target. The default allows at most 5% unusable respondents.

  • min_items: Every scale keeps at least this many items. A scale of the construct that lost all its items counts as 0, so min_items = 1 requires that every scale (or content domain) is still there.

  • min_total: The items number at least this many in all.

  • factors: Parallel analysis over all items finds as many dimensions as there are scales, or one dimension for a construct made with single_scale = TRUE.

Stats from any step can be named, for example the test information of loop_irt() (min = list(marginal_rxx = 0.8)). A stat that no step reports fails, so that a missing check never passes quietly.

See also

revision_loop()

Examples

loop_criterion()
#> function (flags, stats, items, context) 
#> {
#>     rows <- list()
#>     add <- function(name, value, target, pass) rows[[length(rows) + 
#>         1L]] <<- data.frame(criterion = name, value = value, 
#>         target = target, pass = pass, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
#>     if (no_failing_items) {
#>         n <- length(unique(flags$item[flags$severity == "fail" & 
#>             !is.na(flags$item)]))
#>         add("no_failing_items", n, 0, n == 0)
#>     }
#>     for (s in names(min)) {
#>         v <- stats$value[stats$stat == s]
#>         v <- if (length(v) && any(!is.na(v))) 
#>             min(v, na.rm = TRUE)
#>         else NA_real_
#>         add(paste0("min_", s), v, min[[s]], !is.na(v) && v >= 
#>             min[[s]])
#>     }
#>     for (s in names(max)) {
#>         v <- stats$value[stats$stat == s]
#>         v <- if (length(v) && any(!is.na(v))) 
#>             max(v, na.rm = TRUE)
#>         else NA_real_
#>         add(paste0("max_", s), v, max[[s]], !is.na(v) && v <= 
#>             max[[s]])
#>     }
#>     con <- context$construct
#>     if (!is.null(min_items)) {
#>         sc <- unique(c(names(con$scales), items$scale))
#>         n <- min(table(factor(items$scale, levels = sc)))
#>         add("min_items", n, min_items, n >= min_items)
#>     }
#>     if (!is.null(min_total)) 
#>         add("min_total", nrow(items), min_total, nrow(items) >= 
#>             min_total)
#>     if (factors) {
#>         v <- stats$value[stats$stat == "n_factors_all"][1]
#>         k <- if (isTRUE(con$single_scale)) 
#>             1L
#>         else length(unique(items$scale))
#>         add("factors", v, k, !is.na(v) && v == k)
#>     }
#>     if (!length(rows)) 
#>         return(NULL)
#>     do.call(rbind, rows)
#> }
#> <bytecode: 0x64eeefb623f0>
#> <environment: 0x64eee388af48>
#> attr(,"label")
#> [1] "no failing items; alpha >= 0.8; own_scale >= 0.9; careless_share <= 0.05; at least 3 items per scale"
loop_criterion(min = list(alpha = 0.7), factors = TRUE)
